# usrsctp

[sctplab/usrsctp](https://github.com/sctplab/usrsctp) · OSS-Fuzz: [projects/usrsctp](https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/bd2ce21991a94a362b92fb1bf25f86d5a1a60842/projects/usrsctp)

**Status: available.** 3 of OSS-Fuzz's 3 fuzz targets have statements. 12 binaries, 13 MB. 39 statements: 0 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 0 blocked by the model, 39 open.

Built from usrsctp (commit `fd070e05`) with 1 patch, listed under [How these binaries were built](#how-these-binaries-were-built).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fuzzer_connect](fuzzer_connect/) | Client socket, connect, optionally injects canned INIT-ACK / COOKIE-ACK / DATA per data[0] bits, then injects data[1..] as one SCTP packet behind a canned common header; nothing about the processing of that packet is checked. | 1 check (api-contract; 1 weak; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 13 |
| [fuzzer_fragment](fuzzer_fragment/) | Establishes an association with canned INIT-ACK (optionally NR-SACK) and COOKIE-ACK, then splits the input into length-prefixed chunks, injecting each as a packet (optionally sending 4 KiB of data first); nothing about the result is checked. | none | 13 |
| [fuzzer_listen](fuzzer_listen/) | A listening server socket (set up once) receives the whole input (8..65535 bytes) as one raw SCTP packet; the accept upcall only closes the new socket. | none | 13 |

Not included: **api-driver** (held from this release).

## What the statements say, for usrsctp
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.
- **`<build>_disagrees_at_most b`**: for inputs drawn from the harness's `Distribution.v`, the plain and sanitizer builds disagree with probability at most *b*.
- **`<build>_agreement_decidable`**: some riscv64 program decides exactly the finite inputs on which the two builds agree. A program that does so, with a bound on how often it rejects, is a route to a disagreement bound (docs/statements.md).

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch usrsctp
    ./oft verify-sha usrsctp

By hand: download `usrsctp-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/usrsctp/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [sctplab/usrsctp](https://github.com/sctplab/usrsctp) at `fd070e05a7474f38c7fecdf4d4b6005d2547ee00`, built with CMake:
  - 1 patch, whose text is not in this release yet (it ships in the source bundle)
- Harnesses: the harness files are modified in `fuzzer_connect`, `fuzzer_fragment` and `fuzzer_listen` (see each harness page)
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.
